record.question: "The Mizo Chieftainship originated and developed on its own without the influence from outside". Which of the following is the main reason for the rise of chieftainship in the early Mizo society?
options: It is their traditional way of life since time immemorial.
In the traditional period Mizo are semi-nomadic and they were often in conflicts with other clan over land which eventually urged the need to have leader who will lead them at times like this.
The existence of some form of open social hierarchy necessitated the establishment of chieftainship among the Mizo.
